_readme: EMC x TSC1/TSC2, ROUND 4, 2026-08-24 -- THE MEASUREMENT. Round 2 established that cBioPortal's sarcoma_msk_2022 contains 75 samples typed 'Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma' out of 7,494, and msk_impact_50k_2026 contains 15 out of 54,281. That is an order of magnitude more sequenced EMC than any published series (the largest this repository holds is six). Round 4 reads TSC1 and TSC2 status for those samples. Entrez ids are taken from the API's own /genes lookup in round 2, not from recollection: TSC1=7248, TSC2=7249. Round 2's mutations call returned HTTP 400 'Request parameter is missing: entrezGeneId', which is why these are per-gene; and 'Molecular profile not found: sarcoma_msk_2022_cna', which is the finding that sarcoma_msk_2022 carries NO copy-number profile at all -- so that cohort can answer 'TSC1/TSC2 MUTATION' and cannot answer 'TSC2 GENE LOSS', which is the alteration class the index case actually reported. msk_impact_50k_2026 does carry a discrete CNA profile (gistic), so it can. THE PANEL ROWS ARE THE CONTROL AND ARE NOT OPTIONAL: a count of zero mutations is only a reading of absence if the genes were on the panel that was run. The gene-panel rows establish whether TSC1 and TSC2 are sequenced at all by the MSK-IMPACT panels these cohorts use. Without them a zero means 'not looked for', which is a different statement and the one this repository has a standing rule about.
